title: Record Checker
summary: Documented regulatory actions, court rulings, and formal findings, each tied to a named public source. This holds only what the public record shows. Absence of a record is not evidence of good practice.

findings.name: JBS
findings.finding: NY Attorney General sued JBS USA (Feb 2024) over its 'Net Zero by 2040' marketing. Separately, JBS USA agreed a US$4M settlement with the US Department of Labor (Jan 2025) over child labour by its third-party sanitation contractors, funding remediation rather than paying a penalty, and agreed to compliance training and a dedicated specialist.
findings.src: NY Attorney General; US Department of Labor settlement.

findings.name: TotalEnergies
findings.finding: Paris Judicial Court ruled (23 Oct 2025) that its 'carbon neutrality by 2050' consumer marketing was a misleading commercial practice, the first such ruling against a major oil company. The court dismissed the remainder of the NGOs' claims.
findings.src: Paris Judicial Court, judgment of 23 October 2025.

findings.name: Shein
findings.finding: Italy's competition authority fined Infinite Styles Services Co. Ltd — the Dublin company running Shein's European site — €1M (July 2025) for vague, misleading and omissive environmental claims, including emissions targets contradicted by Shein's own rising 2023-24 emissions.

findings.name: KLM
findings.finding: Amsterdam District Court ruled (20 March 2024) that 15 of 19 of KLM's environmental advertising claims were misleading, covering sustainable aviation fuel and reforestation as well as offsetting. No penalty was imposed and no injunction granted, the claims having already been withdrawn.

findings.name: L'Oréal
findings.finding: Not certified under Cruelty Free International's Leaping Bunny programme. L'Oréal states it has not tested its products on animals since 1989, no longer tests ingredients, and tolerates no exception — while noting that some health authorities, notably in China, may themselves conduct tests on cosmetic products.
findings.src: L'Oréal published position; Leaping Bunny certified-brand list.

findings.name: Boohoo
findings.finding: An independent review by Alison Levitt QC (24 Sept 2020) found many failings in Boohoo's Leicester supply chain, including underpayment, and that the company ignored warnings. The same review expressly found Boohoo did not deliberately allow those conditions, did not intentionally profit from them, and that its business model is not founded on exploiting workers.
findings.src: Independent Review into the boohoo Group PLC's Leicester supply chain (Levitt, 2020).

findings.name: Mobilewalla
findings.finding: US FTC finalised an order (Jan 2025) banning the data broker from selling sensitive location data, including visits to health facilities and places of worship.

findings.name: Gravy Analytics / Venntel
findings.finding: US FTC action (Dec 2024) banning the sale of sensitive location data; the companies processed billions of location signals daily from ~1 billion devices.

findings.name: H&M
findings.finding: A US class action (Commodore v. H&M, 2022) alleged the 'Conscious Collection' and its Higg-based 'sustainability profiles' were misleading, and H&M withdrew the scorecards after the underlying data was challenged. The case was voluntarily dismissed with prejudice in December 2023. No finding was made against H&M.
findings.src: Commodore v. H&M (S.D.N.Y.), voluntarily dismissed with prejudice, 13 December 2023.

findings.name: Zara / Inditex
findings.finding: Remains within the EU Consumer Protection Cooperation Network's review scope; watchdogs flagged product terms ('natural', 'sustainable fabric') now restricted under EU rules. No formal EU sanction published as of 2026 — scrutiny ongoing.
findings.src: EU CPC Network; Business & Human Rights Resource Centre

findings.name: Nike
findings.finding: Named in a 2025 report (The Missing Thread) for bold decarbonisation pledges that omit protections for supply-chain workers affected by the shift — 'greenwashing' by exclusion of labour.

findings.name: Sunday Riley
findings.finding: Settled with the US FTC over fake reviews — the CEO and staff posted reviews of their own products on Sephora.com and used a VPN to evade detection. Settlement reached; no admission of fault.

findings.name: Grande Cosmetics
findings.finding: Settled a US class action for US$6.25M over a failure to disclose that its lash, brow and hair serums contain isopropyl cloprostenate, a prostaglandin analogue alleged to carry undisclosed side-effect risks. Final approval July 2024. Settled without admitting wrongdoing; the company maintains its products are safe.

findings.name: Sephora
findings.finding: Agreed to pay US$775,000 (2025) to settle California claims over improper hazardous-waste disposal. Note: a separate suit alleging its 'Clean at Sephora' label was misleading was dismissed in 2024 — the court found no deception.
findings.src: California settlement (2025); NY federal court dismissal (2024)

findings.name: Yves Rocher
findings.finding: Under examination by Paris judges over France's corporate duty-of-vigilance law, concerning alleged labour violations in Turkey. A ruling is expected in 2026 — this is a pending case, not a finding.

findings.name: Coca-Cola, Nestlé, Kraft Heinz & others
findings.finding: Named in a San Francisco lawsuit (Dec 2025) alleging deceptive marketing of ultra-processed foods, including health-oriented messaging and child-directed branding, under California's Unfair Competition Law. Pending — allegations, not proven; companies dispute the claims.
findings.src: City of San Francisco lawsuit (2025), pending

findings.name: Kroger
findings.finding: Subject of a 2024 class action alleging eggs labelled 'Farm Fresh' came from chickens in industrial confinement. A documented labelling dispute — consult the case for the current status.

findings.name: Walmart
findings.finding: Named in a 2024 case alleging salmon marketed as 'sustainable' was deceptively labelled. A documented labelling dispute — consult the case for the current status.

findings.name: Canada Goose
findings.finding: After a PETA complaint to the US FTC, the company stopped making claims that its standards ensured suppliers didn't abuse animals. It pledged to end fur use (2021/2022) but faced continued campaigns over down sourcing. Mix of regulatory outcome + ongoing advocacy scrutiny.
findings.src: US FTC complaint outcome; PETA campaigns

findings.name: Patagonia
findings.finding: Twice suspended wool purchasing after PETA exposés documented cruelty at approved 'responsible wool' suppliers that violated the brand's own welfare standards. Advocacy-sourced investigation; the brand has responded and changed suppliers.

findings.name: Estée Lauder
findings.finding: A federal judge (SDNY) declined to dismiss a securities-fraud suit alleging the company misled investors about the sustainability of its China sales through gray-market 'daigou' resellers, finding actionable half-truths in its disclosures. Estée Lauder later agreed a US$210M settlement with investors, without admitting liability or wrongdoing. An investor-disclosure matter, not a product claim.
findings.src: In re The Estée Lauder Companies Inc. Securities Litigation, 1:23-cv-10669 (S.D.N.Y.).
